question: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treats paracetamol overdose primarily by directly neutralising NAPQI; it works even when given more than 24 hours after ingestion.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. NAC replenishes hepatic glutathione so that endogenous glutathione can detoxify NAPQI; it does not directly neutralise it. Timing is critical: give within 8–10 hours for maximum hepatoprotection. After 24 hours, benefit is uncertain.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This statement is false on both counts. NAC works by replenishing glutathione stores (not by directly neutralising NAPQI), and it is most effective within the first 8–10 hours; beyond 24 hours, hepatic necrosis is established and NAC's benefit is markedly reduced (though it may still be given in fulminant hepatic failure).
